## Description

entries.content:
# Story 3.8 — Crash recovery & graceful shutdown

## Description

Make the worker survive `kill -9`, OOM-killer, host reboot, and `SIGTERM`

  and the process exits within `shutdown_grace_sec` (default 120 s).

entries.content:
# Story 6.5 — Backoff and retry

## Description

Transient failures should retry; permanent ones should stop wasting CPU.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed job whose `attempts < max_attempts` is **not** failed

- Backoff is `min(60 × 2^(attempts-1), 3600) ± 25%` jitter — i.e.,

# Story 6.8 — Graceful shutdown semantics

## Description

The whole queue layer must shut down cleanly on `SIGTERM` so that no
running job is forgotten in `claimed`/`running` state.

entries.title: Personal Access Token (PAT) management
entries.content:
# Story 11.13 — Personal Access Token (PAT) management

**Status:** **NEW** — added in response to
[REVIEW §3.4](../../REVIEW.md): Story 11.6 ("PAT management for clients")
referenced an API surface that no story owned. This story owns it
end-to-end.

A Personal Access Token is a long-lived bearer credential that a user
issues from Settings → Account → Tokens for use by automation, third-party
clients, or scripts. PATs are scoped, named, and revocable. They are
never auto-issued; they always represent an explicit user action.

**Anchors:** [`architecture.md` §9.8 (auth)](../../architecture.md)

entries.content:
# Story 24.5 — Backup and restore

Every state-bearing surface has a documented, tested backup and
restore procedure.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. **Postgres:** daily `pg_dump --format=custom` to a configured
  backup root; retention configurable (default 14 days); a
  `maktaba-api restore --from <file>` command runs `pg_restore` with
  conflict-safe options.
- AC2. **SQLite:** daily `VACUUM INTO` snapshot; restore is a file
  copy.
- AC3. **ChromaDB:** documented as recoverable from the source media
  + transcripts (rebuild via `reprocess --from-stage index`); not
  separately backed up un

entries.title: Disaster recovery
entries.content:
# Story 24.6 — Disaster recovery

Documented recovery scenarios with verified RTO/RPO targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. Recovery scenarios documented with steps and expected wall-
  clock:
  1. **DB lost, media intact** — restore from latest backup;
     reprocess any new media since the backup. RTO ≤ 30 minutes.
     RPO ≤ 24 h (last daily backup).
  2. **DB and derived caches lost, media intact** — same as #1
     plus full reindex. RTO ≤ proportional to library size,
     reported per-library.
  3. **Media partially corrupted** — content_hash on
     mismatch detects; the affected vi

entries.title: Integrity verification
entries.content:
# Story 24.7 — Integrity verification

Periodic and on-demand integrity checks across the canonical surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. A `maktaba-pipeline doctor --integrity` runs:
  - `content_hash` re-verification on a configurable sample (or
    full library, opt-in).
  - Sidecar presence check (every `READY` video has expected
    artifacts).
  - DB referential integrity (no dangling FKs, no soft-deleted
    children with live parents).
  - FTS / Chroma row-count parity with `segments` row count.
- AC2. Integrity reports are written to `audit_log`
  ([Story 21.6](../21-observability

entries.title: Identity stability across operations
entries.content:
# Story 24.8 — Identity stability across operations

`content_hash` is the system-wide identity. Every flow that touches a
file must preserve identity correctly.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. `content_hash = BLAKE3(first 4 MiB || last 4 MiB || u64_le(size))`
  with documented tie-breaker for files smaller than 8 MiB (the
  whole file is hashed once).
- AC2. Identity is computed once on first scan and stored on the
  `videos` row; subsequent scans reuse the stored hash if `(path,
  size, mtime)` is unchanged.
- AC3. Move / rename within a tracked root preserves the hash and
  updates the path

entries.title: Forward and backward compatibility
entries.content:
# Story 24.9 — Forward and backward compatibility

State produced by version N must be readable by N+1 (and reasonably
by N-1 across one minor version), so upgrades and rollbacks
([Epic 22.6](../22-devops/story-22-06-upgrade-rollback.md)) don't
corrupt data.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. Schema changes follow the documented playbook: add column
  nullable → backfill → set NOT NULL in a later release. A single
  release never introduces "breaking" reads of old rows.
- AC2. Generated artifact formats (segment JSON, sidecars) carry a
  `schema_version` field; readers tolerate higher minor versi

entries.title: Implementation Plan Review — Epic 25 (Cloud Relay)
entries.content: Review of all 36 Cloud Relay implementation plans against architecture.md §13 and the matching stories. 4 BLOCKED + 22 NEEDS_REVISION + 10 PASS at the time of writing; all resolved before Phase 17 merge.

entries.title: Full Implementation Audit — All 25 Epics
entries.content: End-to-end audit of `main` (post-merge of #12) against the 272 story acceptance criteria. Surfaced 5 blockers, 8 majors, 11 minors; tracks which were resolved in the audit-blockers cleanup PR (#19).

entries.title: Test Results — main snapshot
entries.content: Full test suite executed across every service after pulling latest `main`. Go (api, streaming, cloud, shared) — green. Pipeline pytest — 810/812 (2 known failures: pyyaml dev-extra). Web typecheck — green. Migration-lint — 11 findings.

entries.title: Phase 1 — Pipeline foundations — Scanner
entries.content: Epic 1: file discovery, BLAKE3 content identity, filesystem watcher, manual control, schema decisions, video state machine.

entries.title: Phase 2 — Pipeline foundations — Audio + Transcription start
entries.content: Epics 2-3 audio extraction (probe, track selection, stream extraction, resource accounting) and the transcription backend protocol + initial backends.

entries.title: Phase 3 — Pipeline foundations — Subtitles + Search
entries.content: Epics 4-5: subtitle generation, FTS via tsvector, Chroma vector backend, hybrid RRF, incremental indexing, query suggestions, chapter inference.

entries.title: Phase 4 — Job queue + Pipeline daemon wiring
entries.content: Epic 6 durable job queue with claim loop, heartbeat, pause/resume/cancel, backoff, reaper, concurrency caps, graceful shutdown.

entries.title: Phase 5 — Subtitles + Search indexing closeout
entries.content: Phase 5 closed out Epics 4-5 and validated the cross-epic search RRF + subtitle live-VTT contract integration.

entries.title: Phase 6 — API server (Epic 7)
entries.content: API CRUD/search/sessions/settings — HTTP skeleton, cursor pagination, library CRUD, ingest endpoints, GraphQL SDL, gRPC clients to Pipeline + Streaming.

entries.title: Phase 7 — Streaming service (Epic 8)
entries.content: HLS/DASH origin: signed-URL gating, capability matrix, direct play, remux, hwaccel, gRPC session lifecycle, subtitle/chapter/poster/sprite cache.

entries.title: Phase 8 — Library management (Epic 9)
entries.content: Library config schema, multi-root overlap detection, ignore rules, periodic sweep, content-hash dedup, manual scan controls, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 9 — Auth & security hardening (Epic 10)
entries.content: User store, web/native login, RS256 + JWKS, signed URLs, single-user mode, CSRF, brute-force + rate limiting, transport security, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 10 — Web UI (Epic 11)
entries.content: React 18 PWA: library browse, video detail, player with transcript, search results, settings, auth flows. Shared with Capacitor/Tauri wrappers.

entries.title: Phase 11 — Mobile + desktop shells (Epics 12-13)
entries.content: Capacitor wrappers (iOS/Android) with native plugins for background download, file association, push, native player handoff. Tauri 2 desktop wrapper.

entries.title: Phase 12 — TV apps + discovery (Epics 14-15)
entries.content: Native tvOS (Swift / AVPlayer) + Android TV (Kotlin / ExoPlayer). mDNS discovery, QR pairing, LAN-first connection flow.

entries.title: Phase 13 — Subscriptions + UX design system (Epics 16-17)
entries.content: Local subscriptions (sources, schedules, RSS, podcast), and the cross-platform design system (tokens, components, motion, RTL).

entries.title: Phase 14 — Performance + scalability (Epics 18-19)
entries.content: Performance budgets, caching, lazy hydration, scalability targets, single-box 30TB validation, worker concurrency tuning.

entries.title: Phase 15 — Testing + observability (Epics 20-21)
entries.content: Test pyramid with tier budgets and CI enforcement, OpenTelemetry traces + metrics, structured logs, error envelopes, health/readiness probes.

entries.title: Phase 16 — DevOps + security + data integrity (Epics 22-24)
entries.content: CI pipelines, container images, migrations infra, security hardening, supply chain, atomic writes, idempotent jobs, backup/restore, disaster recovery.

entries.title: Phase 17 — Cloud Relay (Epic 25)
entries.content: Maktaba Cloud SaaS layer: identity, server claim, WSS tunnel, HTTP relay proxy, bandwidth metering, Stripe billing, push fanout, admin consoles, installers, entitlement signing.
